“Set against unprecedented cost inflation and somewhat weaker than anticipated converting volumes, our third quarter performance of Adjusted EBITDA 1 of $1,205 million with an Adjusted EBITDA Margin 1 of 14.8% represents a resilient performance.
We have also implemented significant pricing initiatives across most paper grades and we expect these should more than offset input costs as these increases are passed through.
This expected outcome primarily reflects the continued and unprecedented cost inflation we are experiencing.
For example, for the full year 2026 we expect to absorb approximately $700 million of additional freight and energy costs alone, significantly more than anticipated.
We have, and are, implementing price increases to more than offset these costs, the full benefits of which we expect to realize into 2027.

We have not reconciled Adjusted EBITDA outlook to the most comparable GAAP outlook because it is not possible to do so without unreasonable efforts due to the uncertainty and potential variability of reconciling items, which are dependent on future events and often outside of management’s control and which could be significant.
Because such items cannot be reasonably predicted with the level of precision required, we are unable to provide an outlook for the comparable GAAP measure (net income).
